lines.cap: **Narrator:** This is Kavya. She is twelve. It is one p.m., thirty-four degrees, and she has just bought chicken rice.
**Kavya:** I have a Science test on digestion tomorrow. So I'm eating. That counts as revision.
**Narrator:** But this documentary is not about Kavya. It is about the long, dark tube her lunch is about to go down.
**Narrator:** The **Alimentary Line**. Seven stations. One direction. No refunds.
**Narrator:** And this is the man who runs it.
**Percy:** Percy. Short for **peristalsis**.
**Percy:** People ask where the trains are. There are no trains. The tunnel is a muscle. The muscle is me.
**Percy:** I squeeze behind the food and push it along. Like toothpaste. All the way to the other end.
**Percy:** We don't talk about the other end.
**Narrator:** Percy has worked the line for twelve years. Every meal. Every curry puff.
**Percy:** She once had four curry puffs in one recess. I still think about it.
**Narrator:** Mind the Gut. Episode four: The Chicken Rice Express.
**Percy:** Passenger check. A **balanced diet** has all seven nutrient groups, in the **right amounts**.
**Percy:** **C**razy **P**eople **F**ind **V**ery **M**any **F**ish **W**et. Carbohydrates, proteins, fats, vitamins, minerals, fibre, water.
**Kavya:** There's no fish. It's chicken rice.
**Percy:** The fish is a memory trick, Kavya. Keep up.
**Percy:** Rice: **carbohydrates**, your **main energy source**. Chicken: **protein**, for **growth and repair**.
**Percy:** The rice is cooked in chicken fat. **Fats** store energy, keep you warm, and protect organs.
**Kavya:** Hang on. Isn't fat bad for you?
**Percy:** Fat isn't bad. Eating far **more energy** than you use is the problem.
**Percy:** Three cucumber slices: **vitamins** and **minerals**, needed in tiny amounts. And her.
**Phoebe:** Hi. Phoebe. **Fibre**. Nobody can digest me. I just... go through.
**Percy:** The soup: **water**, the solvent for your reactions. Water and fibre give no energy, but both are **essential**.
**Narrator:** If a nutrient is missing for a long time, the line posts a service disruption: a **deficiency disease**.
**Percy:** No **vitamin C**: **scurvy**. Bleeding gums. Wounds heal slowly.
**Percy:** No **vitamin D** or **calcium**: **rickets**. Soft, bent bones.
**Percy:** No **iron**: **anaemia**. Too few red blood cells. Tired and pale.
**Phoebe:** No fibre: **constipation**. That one's about me. Nobody says thank you.
**Percy:** They're caused by a **lack** of something, not a germ. You can't catch them. Don't blame the passengers.
**Narrator:** Energy needs vary with **age**, how **active** you are, **size**, **sex**, and **pregnancy**.
**Kavya:** I'm growing. I need more energy. Uncle! Can I upsize?
**Percy:** Upsize the cucumber. No single food has everything. **Variety**, Kavya.
**Narrator:** Station one: the **mouth**. This is where digestion **begins**.
**Percy:** Teeth do **mechanical digestion**: smaller pieces, but no chemical change.
**Percy:** **Incisors** cut. **Canines** grip and tear. **Premolars** and **molars** crush and grind.
**Percy:** Smaller pieces have a bigger **surface area**, so chemical digestion goes faster.
**Amy:** Which is where I come in! Hiii! I'm Amy! **Amylase**! I'm an **enzyme**! I live in the saliva!
**Percy:** Amy has one job. She is very, very excited about it.
**Amy:** **Starch** into **sugars**! Starch is a long chain, and I snip it!
**Amy:** Snip! Snip! Snip!
**Percy:** **Chemical digestion**: enzymes breaking the bonds inside molecules. It starts here too.
**Kavya:** Is that why a plain cracker goes sweet if you keep it in your mouth?
**Amy:** YES! That's me! You can TASTE me working!
**Narrator:** Why bother? Starch, protein and fat are **large, insoluble** molecules: too big to pass through the gut wall.
**Percy:** So they're broken into **small, soluble** molecules, which can be **absorbed**.
**Percy:** Tongue and saliva roll it into a soft, slippery ball: a **bolus**.
**Percy:** Doors closing. Next station: the **oesophagus**.

chapters.title: The squeeze and the acid spa

lines.cap: **Narrator:** The **oesophagus**: the tube down to the stomach. Percy's favourite stretch.
**Percy:** Waves of muscle squeeze behind the food and push it along. **Peristalsis**. Me.
**Kavya:** Doesn't gravity just do that?
**Percy:** No. You could eat upside down and I'd still get it there. Don't test that.
**Narrator:** Next: the **stomach**, a muscular bag that **churns** food and adds **acid**.
**Priya:** Welcome to the acid spa. I'm Priya. **Protease**.
**Priya:** I break **protein** into **amino acids**. The chicken? Mine.
**Percy:** Priya calls it a spa. It's acid. Nobody else calls it a spa.
**Kavya:** So the acid digests the food?
**Priya:** No. Acid **kills harmful microbes**, and gives me the **acidic** conditions I need. I do the digesting.
**Kavya:** Then why doesn't the stomach digest itself?
**Percy:** A thick layer of slimy **mucus**. And it replaces its lining every few days.
**Narrator:** Amy and Priya are **enzymes**: **biological catalysts**. They **speed up** reactions, without being **used up**.
**Priya:** We're not alive. We're molecules. A million proteins today. No breaks. No lunch.
**Priya:** Each enzyme is **specific**. Only protein fits my **active site**, like a key in a lock.
**Amy:** I tried to snip the chicken once.
**Priya:** Didn't fit.
**Percy:** It's not all done here. Digestion **starts** in the mouth, and **finishes** in the small intestine.
**Phoebe:** Still not digested. If anyone was wondering.
**Narrator:** Next: the **small intestine**. Here, digestion **finishes**.
**Bill:** Bill. **Bile**. Made in the **liver**, stored in the **gall bladder**, squirted in here.
**Amy:** Bill's my favourite enzyme!
**Bill:** I'm not an enzyme.
**Bill:** Every day. 'Bill the enzyme.' I don't break any bonds. I'm basically washing-up liquid.
**Lionel:** And I'm Lionel. **Lipase**. I break **fats** into **fatty acids and glycerol**.
**Lionel:** Fatty acids AND glycerol. Both. Every time. Write both.
**Lionel:** But this fat is one enormous blob. I can only work on the outside.
**Bill:** Stand back. I **emulsify** it: big blobs into tiny droplets. Much more **surface area**.
**Lionel:** Now I work much faster. Bill doesn't digest the fat. I do.
**Bill:** And I'm **alkaline**. I **neutralise** the stomach acid, so the enzymes here can work.
**Priya:** I heard that.
**Narrator:** The **pancreas** sends in enzymes too: more amylase, protease and lipase.
**Amy:** More of me! Hello, me!
**Percy:** Liver, gall bladder, pancreas: food never goes through them. They're **not** part of the alimentary canal.
**Bill:** I've never once been on the line. I commute.
**Narrator:** Starch is now **glucose**, protein is **amino acids**, and fat is **fatty acids and glycerol**.
**Phoebe:** I'm still here.
**Narrator:** Meanwhile, in Kavya's Science lesson: food tests. Each one gives a **colour change**.
**Kavya:** Starch: add orange-brown **iodine**. With starch, it turns **blue-black**.
**Amy:** Blue-black! That's starch! Mine!
**Percy:** Iodine **starts** orange-brown, and stays that way with no starch. Don't write it backwards.
**Kavya:** Sugar: blue **Benedict's solution**...
**Kavya:** Nothing's happening.
**Percy:** You have to **heat** it, Kavya. In a water bath. No heat, no result.
**Narrator:** Blue, green, yellow, orange... **brick-red**. A reducing sugar.
**Kavya:** Protein: **biuret** solution. Blue to **purple**.
**Priya:** Purple. Protein. Mine.
**Kavya:** Fat: shake it with **ethanol**, pour it into water. A **cloudy white emulsion**.
**Bill:** An emulsion! That's my move!
**Lionel:** It's still my fat.
**Narrator:** Stronger colour, more nutrient. And a **control**, water with no food, shows what 'negative' looks like.
**Kavya:** Four tests. Four colours. And everyone inside me yelling 'mine'. I have enzymes with opinions.

chapters.title: Vinny and the end of the line

lines.cap: **Narrator:** Back in the small intestine, millions of tiny, finger-like **villi** **absorb** the molecules. One is a **villus**.
**Percy:** This is Vinny. Vinny is a villus. Vinny doesn't talk. Vinny absorbs.
**Percy:** **Big**: a huge **surface area**. Spread flat, the lining covers about **30 m²**. Half a badminton court.
**Percy:** **Thin**: a wall just **one cell thick**. A short trip into the blood.
**Percy:** **Bloody**: a good **blood supply**. **Capillaries** carry the glucose and amino acids away.
**Percy:** And a **lacteal** in the middle, for the products of **fat** digestion.
**Kavya:** Big, Thin, Bloody, Lacteal. That sounds like a horror film.
**Narrator:** What's left moves on to the **large intestine**, which absorbs most of the remaining **water**.
**Phoebe:** And this is me. I give the leftovers **bulk**, so Percy has something to push.
**Percy:** Without Phoebe, I'm squeezing nothing. She stops **constipation**.
**Phoebe:** I'm... useful?
**Narrator:** The next morning. The waste, **faeces**, waits in the **rectum**, then leaves through the **anus**.
**Narrator:** That's **egestion**: removing **undigested** food that was never absorbed.
**Kavya:** Isn't that called excretion?
**Percy:** No. **Excretion** removes waste made by your body's own reactions, in your cells.
**Percy:** Carbon dioxide, out through your **lungs**. **Urea**, made by the **liver** and removed by the **kidneys**, in urine.
**Phoebe:** Well. This is my stop. Goodbye, everyone.
**Percy:** This service terminates here. Thank you for riding the Alimentary Line.

chapters.title: The staff save you some marks

lines.cap: **Narrator:** Before the credits, the staff of the line would like to save you some marks.
**Percy:** One. Digestion isn't just the stomach. It starts in the mouth, and finishes in the small intestine.
**Amy:** Two! Benedict's must be **heated**! And iodine goes orange-brown to **blue-black**, not the other way round!
**Priya:** Three. Enzymes aren't alive, and aren't used up. And stomach acid doesn't digest food. I do.
**Bill:** Four. Bile **emulsifies** fat; it doesn't digest it. And liver, gall bladder and pancreas aren't on the line.
**Lionel:** Five. Fat gives fatty acids **and** glycerol. Protein gives **amino acids**.
**Phoebe:** Six. Most leftover water is absorbed in the **large** intestine. And fibre isn't useless. Apparently.
**Kavya:** Seven. You can't catch a deficiency disease. I asked.
**Narrator:** Mind the Gut will return.
**Percy:** Vinny. Anything you'd like to add?
**Vinny:** ...I'm a villus. Singular.
**Amy:** He TALKS!
**Percy:** Don't encourage him.
